governance.audit: every call and every refusal lands on the hash-chained audit log; message bodies are NEVER written to the log (refusals log tool + rule, not content)
governance.batchSemantics: one verified tap opens ONE batch with a hard send allowance; the batch then fires without per-item prompts (per-item asking is itself the violation of the founder's doctrine); exhausted or closed batch refuses
governance.data: message store stays local (upstream SQLite under the bridge's store/ dir); history leaves the machine only through a tool call the operator makes
governance.reads: ambient but audited — reading the owner's own history is not a governed action
governance.sends: GOVERNED ACTION, never ambient: recipient must be a known contact (registered JID or phone) AND the send must draw on an open per-batch founder tap; unknown recipients refuse even inside a batch; CSAM screen on outbound text/captions
governance.tcpa: the TCPA attestation is the founder's legal act alone — the gate records that a batch was tapped, it never attests
